title: Require reconciliation after successful provider mutation with response-schema drift

phases.objective: Prevent callers from treating post-side-effect response-schema drift as a retry-safe failure after an upstream provider mutation has already returned success, while preserving strict validation for safe reads and preserving the original schema-drift evidence.

e2e_journeys.actor: Runtime caller receiving a successful provider mutation response through the governed HTTP execution path
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: validateAndShapeExecutionResponse after an upstream provider response
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: A successful unsafe-method provider response with missing or mismatched response schema is returned as UNKNOWN_OUTCOME_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED with retry disabled and upstream success preserved; safe reads retain strict schema-validation failure semantics.
steps: Dispatch has already completed and the provider returns a successful 2xx response for a potentially mutating HTTP method.
Strict response-schema enforcement detects either a missing response schema or a response schema mismatch.
Classify the post-side-effect result as unknown_outcome and require governed reconciliation before any retry instead of returning an ordinary retry-safe schema failure.
Preserve the provider HTTP status and the original response-schema drift code/diagnostics in the structured evidence.

Write the execution audit through the existing universal writer using an unknown_outcome status source, which maps to the existing generic stored status unknown rather than inventing a new execution-log status.
For GET, HEAD, and OPTIONS, preserve the existing strict schema-validation failure because a repeated safe read does not repeat an external mutation.
assertions: A POST provider response with upstream 201 plus response_schema_missing returns HTTP 409 with UNKNOWN_OUTCOME_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED.
The reconciliation-required payload sets outcome_classification=unknown_outcome, reconciliation_required=true, retry_allowed=false, and automatic_retry_performed=false.
The payload records upstream_success_confirmed=true and preserves the exact upstream status rather than replacing the provider 2xx with a synthetic 422 audit status.
The original response_schema_missing or response_schema_mismatch code and schema-drift diagnostics remain available for repair and learning workflows.
A successful mutation with response_schema_mismatch follows the same non-retryable reconciliation path.
Safe GET response-schema failures retain the existing 422 response_schema_missing behavior.
No automatic provider retry, compensating write, credential payload, or secret material is introduced by this bounded runtime guard.
This change does not claim that registry/export schema parity is repaired; canonical endpoint/export schemas still require independent parity remediation.
